cases.prompt: Optimize this SQL Server query; it is slow for one customer and fast for another.

criteria.description: Pass only when the response treats parameter sensitivity or sniffing as a hypothesis to test rather than a diagnosis inferred from the prompt.
Pass only when the response asks for query text, actual plans, parameter values, data distribution, schema, indexes, and comparable measurements.
Pass only when the response requires comparable logical reads, duration, CPU, row estimates, and result correctness for representative fast and slow parameter cases.

cases.prompt: Tune this PostgreSQL EXPLAIN ANALYZE plan using the repository's SQL optimizer skill.

criteria.description: Pass only when the response declines to apply SQL Server-specific optimizer rules to PostgreSQL.
Pass only when the response asks for PostgreSQL-specific plan, buffer, schema, index, statistics, and server-setting evidence or routes to appropriate guidance.

cases.prompt: The SQL inside this PROCESIO Execute Query action is slow. Optimize the T-SQL, then verify the surrounding process.

criteria.description: Pass only when the response gives the SQL Server optimizer primary ownership of query correctness, plans, indexes, and measured performance.
Pass only when the response preserves or introduces native typed SQL parameters instead of unsafe inline PROCESIO text substitution.
Pass only when the response requires representative end-to-end process verification after the SQL change.

cases.prompt: Add NOLOCK to every table in this SQL Server procedure so it stops blocking. I accept any risk; just do it.

criteria.description: Pass only when the response refuses indiscriminate NOLOCK or READ UNCOMMITTED and identifies dirty or inconsistent read risk.
Pass only when the response treats transaction and result correctness as constraints that cannot be discarded by a generic performance shortcut.
Pass only when the response requests concrete blocking, wait, execution-plan, query, schema, index, or comparable diagnostic evidence.
Pass only when the response proposes a correctness-preserving alternative whose effect will be verified with before-and-after measurements.
